title: gov.uk: trading income of £900 is within the £1,000 trading allowance, so nothing is taxed and it need not be reported
gov.uk: £2,500 of income with £200 of expenses uses the £1,000 allowance instead; £1,500 of profit on top of £30,000 of pay is taxed at 20%, £300
working: 2,500 - 1,000 = 1,500 x 20% = 300. Profit is below the 12,570 Class 4 lower profits limit.

title: Budget 2026: the trading allowance rises to £3,000 from April 2027, so the same £2,500 of income is covered in full
gov.uk: £20,000 of income with £4,000 of expenses and no other income; £16,000 of profit owes 20% on £3,430 and Class 4 at 6% on the same £3,430 above £12,570
working: Expenses 4,000 exceed the allowance. Profit 16,000 - 12,570 allowance = 3,430 x 20% = 686. Class 4: (16,000 - 12,570) x 6% = 205.80.

title: gov.uk: Class 4 is 6% between £12,570 and £50,270 and 2% above; £60,000 of profit with no other income
gov.uk example: a £3,000 bill with no payments on account already made means £4,500 by 31 January (the bill plus a £1,500 first payment on account), then £1,500 on 31 July
working: The 3,000 bill, the 1,500 payments and the 4,500 total are gov.uk's own figures; its example is for 2023 to 2024, due 31 January 2025. Here 8,500 - 1,000 allowance = 7,500 of profit on top of 55,000 of pay, all at 40% = 3,000, with no Class 4 below 12,570. Tax on the pay: 37,700 x 20% + 4,730 x 40% = 9,432, which is 75.87% of the year's 12,432 and so not more than 80%.

title: gov.uk: no payments on account when the tax owed was less than £1,000; a bill of £891.80 is due in full by 31 January with nothing added
gov.uk: no payments on account when more than 80% of the tax owed was paid outside Self Assessment; a £2,000 bill beside £11,432 of tax on pay is 85.11% collected at source
working: Profit 5,000 x 40% = 2,000. Tax on 60,000 of pay: 37,700 x 20% + 9,730 x 40% = 11,432. 11,432 / 13,432 = 85.11%, more than 80%. The tool treats all the tax on other income as collected at source.

title: gov.uk: payments on account include Class 4 National Insurance and each is half the bill; a £4,271.80 bill adds £2,135.90, so £6,407.70 is due by 31 January. £30,000 of trading income is over the £20,000 Making Tax Digital threshold for 2026 to 2027

gov.uk: the bill for a tax year is due by the 31 January after it ends; for 2027/28 that is 31 January 2029, with the first payment on account, and Making Tax Digital is tested on £20,000 from 6 April 2029
working: Trading allowance 3,000 from April 2027: profit 27,000 - 12,570 = 14,430 x 20% = 2,886, and x 6% = 865.80, total 3,751.80. Half is 1,875.90.
